source: Fire Marshal Bill RULES.md, KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md, PATCH_NOTES.md (cleaned)
facts: Video baseline (Oct 29, 2026): Singularity H3 v1.3 int8 on ComfyUI 0.42.5 with the exact-LoRA loader; H3LoadReport must show lossy 0 and its expect field holds layer counts, never strengths.

Video LoRAs: realism 0.7 only if every character in the shot looks human, otherwise 0 (no in-between); character swap v1.5 at 1.0; exactly one speed LoRA, lightx2v 8-step v1.1 at 0.8; no likeness LoRA.
Video sampler: 8 steps, euler / simple, shift 6, seed 77. Rerolls use seeds 78 and 79 only for a bad or errored piece, never for graph or validation errors.
Video GPU: RunPod RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell SECURE at about $2.49/hr, one pod per clip, run in parallel. Stills/refs use RTX A6000 SECURE at about $0.59/hr.

Video refs are separate images (never a sheet): head front (neutral, mouth closed), full body front, and full body back in the same outfit whenever the character is seen from behind; 1536 long side, flat 8-bit RGB, no alpha, ref_image_size max, at most 9 per shot.
Render sizes: 1152x640 for 16:9, 640x1152 vertical, 4:3 sources keep 4:3 at about the same pixel count (960x768 or 1024x768). Native render resolution is the deliverable.
Banned on video: SeedVR2 upscale (looks painted/plastic), ResCascade (H3HiresFix) and Fizgig (FizgigH3Tweaks); also no interpolation, grade, grain, face restore or paste-back.

Every clip keeps the source fps; the driver is muted with no audio inputs in the graph; the source audio is cut to the exact window and muxed back at the same length. Silent deliverables are flagged up front.
Final videos are trimmed to exactly the planned frame count before the audio mux; this removes the frozen padded tail.
Pieces are at most 141 frames, never span a hard cut, and long shots are chained with a 22-frame guide (10-frame hold + 12-frame crossfade at seams).
The luma check fails a clip if most frames have YMAX <= 16 (black) or YMIN >= 235 (washed out); it runs in qc/selfcheck.py post.
There is no audit bot: Bill runs python3 qc/selfcheck.py pre before asking for a yes and qc/selfcheck.py post --clip <id> --live after render, and pastes both PASS/FAIL tables with evidence.
Nothing paid runs without the owner's explicit yes to a quote line 'About $X (cap $Y), about N min.' plus a | Setting | Old | New | what's-different table versus the last run they saw.
No silent changes: any setting off the baseline is named and approved, or fixed instead of launched. OOM or graph errors stop the clip; settings never change on their own.

The budget gate sums every per-pod ledger since budget.start in the job JSON (across ledger_roots) plus the new caps; if the total exceeds the budget nothing launches. Crashed starts are counted once.

Never say a run is live until the pod is confirmed on RunPod. Relay status only on stage changes: LAUNCHED, DOWNLOADING, READY, FIRST OUTPUT, PIECE n/N, ASSEMBLY, TRIM + AUDIO, DONE, FAILED + reason, TERMINATED.
After every run, terminate all pods, confirm 0 remain on RunPod, and report real spend against the cap.

Every shot gets its own prompt naming each subject's position and clothing and each picture's role; include 'match the source's mouth and expression exactly' and 'keep any objects already in the scene; add nothing'; back views get no face words.
The background color is written into the ref generation prompt ('solid pure black #000000 background, evenly black edge to edge'); never generate on another color and matte it afterward.

Ref stills recipe: fresh whites with Qwen-Image 2.1 (25 steps, cfg 1, seed 77) decoded with the texture-fix VAE, real photos as identity inputs; edits to black with Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 (40 steps, cfg 4, shift 3.1), angle LoRA 0.9 only for angles/backs; optional SeedVR2 7B image upscale to 1536 with no face restore.
Plastic skin in refs comes from stacked edits on AI images, fp8 plus the angle LoRA, 1 MP with no detail pass and flat light; the fix is one pass from real photos, texfix on decode.
Faces come from real photos whenever possible; never use a generated image as the main face ref. Check tattoos and marks sit on the correct side of the person's body (selfies are mirrored).

H3 has no mask input and no pose lock: masks (YOLO11m-seg + ByteTrack + SAM2.1-tiny, CPU, $0) are only for writing positions into prompts and checking pieces; the source pose and arms win over the prompt, so choose a different window instead.
With 3 or more characters in one shot H3 can swap heads; prefer fewer characters per shot or a calmer window, and offer SCAIL-2 (20 steps, less photoreal) only with the owner's OK.

Measured PRO 6000 piece times: one person 141 frames at 960x768 about 340 s (~$0.24); two people with 4 refs at 1120x640 about 450-480 s (~$0.32). Oct 29 15-second clips cost $1.12-$1.74 each; pod boot is about 12 min.
Memory: 6 refs at 1536 fit on the PRO 6000; 9 refs at 2048 on a 3-character shot went out of memory.

The default GPU image ghcr.io/ayoomeco/genie-jutsu-worker:fastboot-comfy-0.42.5-r2 is public and pulls with no token; models download at boot with sha256 checks. Build image/Dockerfile and set GJ_IMAGE only for a private build.

Deliver with phone-friendly Dropbox view links (never folder paths): final, side-by-side with sides named, QC sheet, self-check tables, spend vs cap and flags. Big files use a temporary upload link plus one curl POST, never chunked uploads.
Phone-safe encode: H.264 High 4.2, yuv420p, bt709, AAC, +faststart.

Every job gets a record in Dropbox: README (what, why, recipe, what's different, spend, problems, results, file map, open decisions), a recipe/ folder with configs and logs (no keys), and one line in JOB_INDEX.md.
Before re-asking the owner anything or saying 'can't', check the patch notes, knowledge base, job index and memory; save each new owner decision to memory and the patch notes the same turn.
Keys (RUNPOD_API_KEY, DROPBOX_TOKEN, HF_TOKEN) are collected only through the secure secret card and read by name; never printed, logged or written to files.
Only consenting people or original characters go into videos; results are private and are never posted or shared without the owner.
A likeness LoRA is not part of the default render; on tests, strengths 0.35-0.68 broke identity, so stack one only as a separate quoted test.
